Time-lagged common cause (e.g., atmospheric tide, diurnal cycle) affecting all instruments with frequency-dependent phase shifts
Unidentified calibration error or instrumental malfunction in resonator instruments
Observer or environmental change specific to the observatory site around day 18
Gravitational or height-dependent systematic offset between lab and observatory, confounded with a real pendulum_obs drift on day 18
Shared environmental driver (temperature, humidity, or tidal forcing) with frequency-dependent phase shifts, now visible as pendulum_obs instability
Measurement protocol or observer competence change at the observatory around day 18 (e.g., timing convention shift, apparatus misalignment, fatigue artifact)
Resonator instruments are miscalibrated or drifting, yielding apparent anti-correlations with pendulums by systematic bias rather than true coupling
Observer or environmental change specific to observatory site around day 18, unrelated to lab
Shared environmental driver (temperature, humidity, or tidal cycle) with frequency-dependent phase delays, causing instrument-specific drift and negative cross-correlations
True gravitational or height offset between observatory and lab sites, plus genuine day-18 drift in pendulum_obs
Measurement protocol or timing-convention change at observatory around day 18 (observer fatigue, apparatus misalignment, or beat-cycle definition shift)
Resonator instruments are miscalibrated or have lower measurement fidelity, producing spurious or misleading correlations
Shared environmental driver (thermal, tidal, or pressure cycle) with instrument-dependent response delays, plus independent local change at observatory around day 18
True gravitational (or height) offset between observatory and lab sites, plus independent observer protocol change or environmental disturbance at observatory around day 18
Observer fatigue, protocol drift, or apparatus misalignment at observatory around day 18 (human factor, not environmental)
Resonator instruments have lower measurement fidelity or systematic calibration error, producing spurious negative cross-correlations with pendulums

Multiple independent phenomena occurring simultaneously: constant g offset between sites + global tidal/thermal cycle with phase delays + local observer protocol change or environmental transient at observatory day 18
Shared environmental driver (thermal, pressure, or tidal cycle) with instrument-dependent phase delays, superimposed on a local observatory perturbation around day 18

True gravitational or elevation offset between observatory and lab sites (~0.49 difference in pendulum period implies ~2% g variation or ~200 m altitude difference), with the day-18 pendulum_obs shift caused by a local environmental transient unrelated to baseline offset

Observer protocol change, apparatus misalignment, or local environmental disturbance at the observatory around day 17–19, causing the pendulum_obs level shift, independent of any global coupling mechanism
Artifact or calibration error in one or both resonator instruments, producing spurious negative correlations when compared to pendulums
Shared environmental driver (thermal, pressure, or tidal cycle) with instrument-dependent phase delays, plus a local observatory perturbation around day 18

True gravitational or elevation offset between observatory and lab sites (~49% period difference in baseline pendulum measurements), with the day-18 shift caused by a local environmental transient unrelated to the baseline offset

Observer protocol change, apparatus misalignment, or local environmental disturbance at the observatory around day 17–19, causing the pendulum_obs level shift, independent of any global coupling mechanism
Artifact or measurement bias in resonator instruments (coarser resolution, averaging window, or calibration drift), producing false negative correlations when compared to pendulums

Unidentified systematic bias or coupling mechanism not yet considered; could involve instrumental resonances, observer-apparatus interaction, or environmental factors with non-linear or threshold behavior
Environmental transient or thermal event localized to observatory on day 34, affecting resonator_obs frequency measurement; unrelated to earlier day-18 pendulum_obs shift or systematic correlations
Calibration drift or intermittent measurement error in resonator_obs electronics or frequency-counting apparatus, unmasked on day 34

The day-18 pendulum_obs level shift and day-34 resonator_obs excursion are coupled symptoms of a slow environmental oscillation (multi-cycle forcing with ~16–20 day period) affecting observatory instruments with different phase delays and amplitudes

Measurement programme baseline is not yet established with sufficient statistical depth; observed anomalies (day-18 shift in pendulum_obs, day-34 excursion in resonator_obs) are within expected variability for n ≤ 200 trials per instrument and require more data before declaring a true anomaly
Apparatus misalignment, thermal stress fracture, or mechanical fatigue in resonator_obs mounting, causing resonant frequency to shift upward on day 34; unrelated to other instruments

Residual: genuine anomaly driven by a mechanism not yet considered (e.g., nonlinear instrument response to compound environmental drivers, observer protocol change specific to day 34, or artifact in data logging/timestamping)
Thermal transient or sustained thermal drift localized to observatory, affecting resonator_obs frequency response
Intermittent or progressive electronics fault in resonator_obs apparatus (gain, reference clock, or frequency-counter calibration drift)

Multi-cycle environmental oscillation (barometric, thermal, or pressure-driven) with ~32-day period and site-specific coupling, causing day-18 pendulum_obs shift and day-34 resonator_obs elevation as separated phases
Baseline epoch insufficient; observed anomalies lie within expected variability for n≤100 trials per instrument; true baseline not yet established
Mechanical misalignment, stress relief, or thermal-induced frequency shift in resonator_obs cavity or mounting
Thermal transient or sustained thermal drift localized to observatory, affecting resonator_obs frequency response
Intermittent or progressive electronics fault in resonator_obs (gain, reference clock, or frequency-counter calibration)
Baseline epoch still insufficient; anomalies lie within plausible variability; reserve judgment until n≥100 post-baseline per instrument
Multi-cycle environmental oscillation (~32-day period) with phase separation 16 days (day 18 → day 34), site-specific coupling to observatory instruments
Mechanical misalignment, stress relief, or thermal-induced frequency shift in resonator_obs cavity or mounting
